Subject: Territory lock priorities, snapshots, and failback plan

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet this morning. Quick recap + agreed next steps from our call focused on data placement and recoverability:

- Goal: Ensure MedSys primary data remains in the US (primary region), allow APAC/EU read-only replicas for latency-sensitive users, and define a clear failback for cross-region incident recovery.
- Questions Sarah raised: PII handling for patient identifiers, retention windows for logs, snapshot encryption + key ownership, and how automated failover interacts with territory constraints.

Action items we agreed on:
1) I’ll share our concise doc that maps RPO/RTO options to pinning and snapshot cadence. (attached — "redwood-data-residency-onepager.pdf")
2) Monica (engineering) to confirm whether snapshots can be stored only in US buckets while still supporting cross-region warm replicas.
3) Ben to provide the SOC2 / audit summary and a one-page encryption note (KMS options + customer-managed keys).
4) Sarah to confirm internal requirements for immutable audit logs vs. normal retention (are 7 years required or 1 year acceptable?).

Next call: Wed 2028-07-14 14:00 PT to review the architecture diagram and pick a preferred pinning profile.

Thanks —
Dylan

Hi all —

Quick technical notes following Dylan's recap:

1) Snapshots and region storage
- We can take application-consistent snapshots of model KV caches + tokens and store snapshot objects in a US-central S3 bucket. Snapshots are encrypted at rest and can be configured to use customer-managed KMS keys (CMK).
- For warm replicas in EU/APAC, we replicate only the model weights and non-PII caches. Snapshot copies containing PII are not replicated unless you explicitly allow cross-region replication.

2) Failover behavior
- Automated failover (for availability) has two modes:
  a) Fast failover (automatic) — immediate routing to the nearest healthy region; this could cross territory boundaries and would require explicit authorization if you must keep traffic within a territory.
  b) Controlled failover (recommended for regulated workloads) — manual or orchestrated via canary traffic and runbooks; RPO depends on snapshot frequency.

3) RPO/RTO options (high level)
- Daily snapshots: RPO ~24h, RTO ~30–60m for service restore (routing + cold start).
- Hourly snapshots with warm caches in US: RPO ~1h, RTO ~10–20m (warm worker pools).
- Synchronous cross-region replication (only for non-PII): near-zero RPO for replicated assets, but not recommended for PII.

4) Audit logs and retention
- Application logs: configurable retention 30–730 days. We can export immutable, append-only audit logs to a US-only bucket for 7-year retention if you require it.

I'll attach a diagram (snapshot-architecture-20280712.png) before our call. Happy to walk the team through it on Wed.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsys.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jose Ramirez <j.ramirez@medsys.com>
Date: 2028-07-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Territory lock priorities, snapshots, and failback plan

Thanks Dylan and Monica — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our security/compliance side:

- Patient identifiers are treated as PII and cannot leave US boundaries unless we have explicit patient-consent flags. So any snapshot that includes those identifiers must remain in US storage only.
- For auditability we need append-only audit logs stored for 7 years; those logs must be inaccessible from EU/APAC unless we pull aggregates.
- KMS: prefer customer-managed keys (we manage keys in our AWS account). Can you outline the steps for CMK integration and whether rotation is supported without breaking snapshot restores?

Also: Can you confirm whether the controlled failover option will allow us to failover compute to an APAC region for read-only traffic while keeping write paths pinned to the US? That's our preferred compromise for latency while preserving data residency.

If you can send a short one-pager on CMK steps, rotation, and the runbook for controlled failover, that would be ideal for our compliance team review.

Regards,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Infrastructure, MedSys Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsys.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-14T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Territory lock priorities, snapshots, and failback plan

Sarah —

Thanks for the clarifications. Couple of deliverables attached and next steps below:

Deliverables (attached):
- SOC2-summary-abridged.docx (high-level controls and cert scope)
- redwood-data-residency-onepager.pdf (Dylan's doc)
- snapshot-architecture-20280712.png (Monica's diagram)

Short answers to your questions:
- CMK integration: we support AWS KMS CMKs via a cross-account key policy and a grant model. Rotation is supported — we re-encrypt new snapshots with the rotated key; existing encrypted snapshot metadata remains intact and we maintain a key alias map so restores continue to work. I'll drop a 1-page CMK steps doc into the Drive link and ping you.
- Controlled failover: yes — routing supports split read/write policies. You can pin write endpoints to US-only and permit read-only replica routing to APAC/EU. Failback runbook will include a validation window and verification steps for data locality.

Next steps:
1) Dylan & Monica: please upload the CMK steps + the runbook to the Drive link by EOD Tues (2028-07-16).
2) Sarah: once you have the docs, can you share the compliance intake form preferred by your audit team so we can crosswalk controls?
3) Schedule: Wed 2028-07-14 14:00 PT remains confirmed — Monica to present the diagram and RPO/RTO tradeoffs.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
